scope: Primary-source review of real EV price/incentive field data. No model fitting, old-data changes, installation, email, access request, account creation, paid access or third-party keys.

priority_conclusion.best_real_incentive_lead: Calgary Show Me the Money! (AEJ Economic Policy 2025) has an official replication package and randomized prospective financial incentives. Public metadata and paper are verified; the main replication files are not acquired this turn because the folder returned errors and the download endpoint redirected to ICPSR login.
priority_conclusion.actually_downloaded_real_ev_data: Harvard Dataverse workplace norms original CSV plus metadata/codebook/README are downloaded and read, CC0 verified. This is real EV session data but is not usable as prospective continuous-price treatment data.
priority_conclusion.continuous_curve_readiness: None of these five reviewed EV sources is presently both acquired at the user/event microdata level and demonstrated to support the required continuously varying prospective compensation with suitable observed outcomes. Do not report a real continuous-compensation curve experiment as completed.
priority_conclusion.next_usable_role: Calgary, if legitimately obtained, can validate effects at randomized reward/no-reward arms and associated timing/energy outcomes. Harvard can test real session parsing/behavior descriptions. Neither validates arbitrary continuous compensation doses or the physical effective response-duration truth used in the current simulator.

sources.title: Show Me the Money! A Field Experiment on Electric Vehicle Charge Timing
sources.publication: American Economic Journal: Economic Policy 17(2), May 2025, 259-284; DOI 10.1257/pol.20230653
sources.evidence: Publisher article page links the replication package. Author-hosted final article sections I-II describe randomization, prospective reward messages, baseline period and vehicle monitoring. Official repository metadata lists V1 published 2025-04-17, study period February-December 2022, and 150 successfully installed monitoring devices out of 217 signups.
sources.prospective_treatment: Reward group offered 3.5 Canadian cents per kWh for charging from 22:00 to 06:00; separate information and control groups. Second phase re-randomizes reward continuation/removal. The stated offer is prospective and is not the later total reward paid.
sources.paper_reported_outcomes: Timestamped charging kWh and maximum kW, home/away location, driving trips/distances; baseline charging and participant survey context. These fields are reported by the paper, not verified as acquired microdata columns this turn.
sources.user_time_randomization: Vehicle/household panel and treatment phases with pretreatment observations are described. Installation pool size is not asserted as the final complete analysis sample.
sources.continuous_amount_support: A fixed reward rate versus no reward with additional nonfinancial arms/phases. This supports discrete randomized contrasts, not a nonparametrically identified response curve over arbitrary continuous amounts.
sources.physical_duration_target: Charging energy/timing can be valid outcomes. No independently labeled counterfactual power-reduction response interval, cumulative effective duration or longest physical response duration has been established.
sources.access_actual: Project metadata and author paper read with web tool. A weather XLSX entry in Data was indexed; this does not establish access to charging microdata. Replication-File folder requests timed out or returned 403. Project download link redirected to ICPSR OAuth login. No account used/created and no main charging data or README acquired.
sources.license_actual: Dataset license/terms for the main files not established from the accessible project overview. Publisher existence is not a blanket reuse license. Do not infer confidential or publicly downloadable without login solely from the overview.
sources.fit_for_current_task: Most promising real randomized EV financial-incentive lead, but access and actual analysis-file fields must still be verified; not ready for the continuous-dose pilot.

sources.title: Replication Data for: A Field Experiment on Workplace Norms and Electric Vehicle Charging Etiquette
sources.license: CC0-1.0 verified in downloaded official latestVersion.license metadata; file restricted=false and fileAccessRequest=false.
sources.acquisition_actual: Official API metadata, original CSV, server-converted TAB, DDI codebook and author README downloaded without account/key. Original CSV MD5 exactly matches official metadata 4dd55954d86ea25f21367d9e8d4f379c.
sources.dictionary_actual: Author README defines dollars as amount paid by a user for a session, charge duration as session hours, userId as an anonymized transaction-linked user, and station/location/facility context. Actual duration column is chargeTimeHrs, whereas README uses chargeTime; the actual file schema takes precedence for parsing.
missing_for_continuous_price_study: No prospective offer, announced price/rate, notification time or randomized price assignment column.
No full user-by-eligible-opportunity panel with explicit zero charging opportunities; rows are observed sessions.
No power/current trajectory, control request time, state of charge, deadline slack or counterfactual baseline.
No label equating session length to effective reduction-response duration.
sources.important_distinction: The 49 distinct observed dollars values are post-session payments, jointly determined by use. They are not 49 randomized or prospective treatment levels, and dollars/chargeTime cannot be manufactured into assigned compensation.
sources.dates_observed: Original CSV itself contains year strings 0014 and 0015; first row created=0014-11-18 15:40:26, and observed created string range ends 0015-10-04. This is present in original downloaded bytes, not solely a TAB conversion. No silent year repair was made.
sources.tab_checksum_note: TAB has the official reported 463157 byte size but its fetched MD5 differs from the original-file MD5 in metadata. The explicitly requested original CSV is 455103 bytes and matches the official original checksum; use the original CSV as the byte-verified source.
sources.fit_for_current_task: Acquired real EV sessions and public data dictionary; useful for descriptive/session pipeline checks. It does not provide the prospective continuous monetary treatment required by part 3. Do not fit a causal continuous-compensation curve using dollars as treatment.

sources.title: Can electric vehicles aid the renewable transition? Evidence from a field experiment incentivizing midday charging
sources.publication: Journal of Public Economics 260, August 2026, 105696; DOI 10.1016/j.jpubeco.2026.105696
sources.primary_evidence: Publisher abstract reports 390 EVs with minute-level tracking and time-based incentive effects. Publisher Data availability explicitly states that the used data are confidential. Registry identifier AEARCTR-0011698 is listed.
sources.reported_data_roles: Treatment windows and actual charging/time/location, driving and battery state responses are relevant to EV flexibility. This is paper-reported design, not acquired raw fields.
sources.access_actual: Publisher page read; no raw user/event observations, codebook or licensed public replication dataset obtained. No author request sent.
sources.continuous_support: Time-based incentive intervention does not by itself establish continuous assigned-compensation support. Microdata inaccessible, so amount distribution and exact mapping are not verified.
sources.fit_for_current_task: Strong contemporary scientific precedent; not an immediately available training/test dataset. Do not present the paper's 390 vehicles as our acquired real sample.

sources.title: Electric vehicle charging at the workplace: Experimental evidence on incentives and environmental nudges
sources.publication: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management 139, August 2026, 103383; DOI 10.1016/j.jeem.2026.103383
sources.primary_evidence: Publisher abstract describes natural field experiment n=629 drivers with randomized time-invariant discounts and environmental nudges. Publisher Data availability says data are confidential. AEA RCT registry explicitly says public data available: No and describes computer individual randomization, large/small discount and subsequent phases.
sources.intervention_match: Prospective price discounts are relevant, but finite large/small treatment levels are not continuous-dose support. Charger scarcity/interference is a substantive variable for interpreting responses.
sources.access_actual: Publisher page and registry read. No microdata/codebook acquired; no request or paid access attempted.
sources.fit_for_current_task: Useful for design and effect-modifier hypotheses; currently inaccessible as a direct real-data experiment. Does not validate physical response duration or our algorithm accuracy.

sources.title: The Impact of Dynamic Prices on Electric Vehicle Public Charging Demand: Evidence from a Nationwide Natural Field Experiment
sources.publication: NBER Working Paper 34600, December 2025; DOI 10.3386/w34600; author PDF dated 2025-12-15
sources.primary_evidence: NBER page and author PDF read. Methods sections 2.2-2.5 describe four sequences of control, green notification, 15% discount and 40% discount, crossover blocks, event windows, pre-notification and baseline use. User-ID modulo sequence assignment is explicitly described by the paper; do not relabel as independently re-randomized continuous offers each event.
sources.reported_inputs_outcomes: Receipt/charging demand, user/event identifiers and baseline charging are described. The paper discusses linked vehicle capacity/context for subsets and special access to charger/smart-meter data. This is not an acquired analysis-file schema.
sources.continuous_support: Two positive randomized percentage-discount levels plus control, not a continuously randomized compensation amount. Absolute charger prices may vary observationally; that variation cannot be equated with randomized continuous rates.
sources.access_actual: NBER page and author-hosted PDF accessible. NBER PDF endpoint and registry fetch returned 403 in this session. No official public microdata or code repository was located in this targeted search, and no data downloaded. The examined author PDF did not contain an explicit confidentiality statement; access is unestablished rather than proven confidential.
sources.physical_duration_target: Charging receipts and quantities are not labeled cumulative effective response duration; the app-level increase also includes substitution across payment platforms, which affects interpretation of outcomes.
sources.fit_for_current_task: Important real price-response evidence and potentially valuable future lead. Not an acquired dataset and not direct continuous-compensation validation at present.

execution_record: Default sandbox network first returned WinError10013. The same public metadata/CC0 downloads were retried through approved network escalation and succeeded. Calgary folder then returned HTTP403 and the browser project-download endpoint required ICPSR login; no bypass attempted. Metadata inspection, field/count checks and hashes only; no causal model, simulation or benchmark fitting.
reporting_rule: Distinguish real data actually acquired, paper-reported real experiments, and simulated performance. Do not use paper participants as our experiment N, post-session dollars as prospective offers, or session duration as physical response duration.
